changes.balance: The market rents the war premium by the night and returns it by the afternoon: Tuesday's dip toward $97 on flows, then confirmed strikes plus a hurricane put the bid back. The premium leaks on intact flows but the floor stays firm without a diplomatic breakthrough.
changes.body: Overnight tape bid: Brent Dec $101.55-101.65 (+~1%), WTI $90.15-90.27 (+~0.9%) into the Singapore morning (The Hindu BusinessLine; ksaexpats live benchmarks). Brent-WTI holding ~$11.4. Two fresh legs: (1) Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation confirmed Houthi strikes damaged Jazan and Najran airports Tuesday, wounding three - the first Riyadh-confirmed hit in this round (Riyadh airport, Rabigh refinery, Abha claims remain unconfirmed); (2) NHC says a Gulf of Mexico storm becomes the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days, over offshore areas producing 15% of US crude and 5% of US gas. Tuesday's session: ICE Brent traded down toward $97 before recovering to settle ~$100.4 (ING). Saudi energy minister: East-West pipeline at 5.8 Mb/d - the Hormuz bypass is full.
changes.conditional: Confirmed strike on Saudi energy infrastructure -> premium rebuilds fast; ceasefire proposal advances -> premium bleeds.
changes.delta: Brent Dec ~$101.6 (+1%), WTI ~$90.2 (+0.9%) overnight; Tuesday Brent dipped to ~$97, settled $100.58; Jazan/Najran strikes confirmed by Riyadh; Gulf hurricane forming
changes.source: The Hindu BusinessLine, Oct 7, 2026; ksaexpats; ING Commodities Feed, Oct 7, 2026; Saudi GACA statement, Oct 6, 2026; Reuters, Oct 6, 2026
changes.title: Overnight tape bid on confirmed strikes and hurricane; Tuesday dipped to $97

changes.balance: The release is the ceiling on the product market; the physical drivers (Russia's diesel export ban through Oct 31, China's October product-export halt) are the floor. A Gulf Coast refining track on the hurricane would tighten the distillate leg further.
changes.body: NYMEX diesel crack settled $102.47 on Tuesday Oct 6 (+$1.00 vs Monday's $101.47) - second straight close above $100 after Friday's $97.94 broke the prior 18-day run (validated against the refreshed crack history; all-time max $117.92, Sep 16; 3-2-1 at $66.18 vs $75.31 max Aug 28). The overnight session print runs ~$106.84 (Yahoo front-month bar ~02:00 MDT - provisional, not a close). ING's gasoil mark ($85->$70) and the G7's front-loaded diesel are the ceiling; Russia's export ban through Oct 31, China's October halt, and Ukrainian refinery strikes are the floor. New from EIA's October STEO (published Tuesday): 2026 Brent spot forecast raised to $96.32 (from $91), Q4 avg $105 on inventory draws, 2026 WTI $88.21; Winter Fuels Outlook flags East Coast distillate 20-30% below the 5-yr seasonal average - the agency's own numbers frame distillate tightness as structural.
changes.conditional: Hurricane tracks into Gulf Coast refining -> distillate tightens hard; front-loaded diesel arrives on schedule -> cracks stay soft into winter.
changes.delta: Diesel crack $102.47 Tuesday close (>$100, second straight); overnight ~$106.84 provisional; 3-2-1 $66.18
changes.source: Validated crack history (Yahoo front-month futures), refreshed Oct 7, 2026; DTN/EIA STEO, Oct 6, 2026
changes.title: Diesel crack extends $100 regime; hurricane adds distillate wrinkle

changes.balance: September's >$20 WCS blowout (widest since Dec 2023) was a refinery-outage event, not an egress event - and it is already unwinding on restarts. The December seasonal wide is starting to price; the Nov-Dec egress crunch trades on the ~Oct 19 apportionment notice.
changes.body: ICE settles Oct 6: TMW Nov26 -$24.44 (-$0.08), Dec26 -$25.25 (-$0.50) - December remains the widest tenor and widened half a dollar. ARV Nov26 -$15.41 (-$0.28), Dec26 -$16.10 (-$0.85). ARV-TMW November spread +$9.04/bbl (implied Hardisty-to-Houston export arb, still healthy). SYN (TMS) Nov26 +$5.82; C5 (TMF) Nov26 +$4.55 (+$0.19); MSW (TMR) Nov26 -$1.59; UHC (TMU) Nov26 +$2.40. The ~700 kb/d PADD 2 demand snap-back stands (Joliet restarted ~Sep 28-Oct 2; Whiting at full strength per Reuters Sep 21); today's 10:30 a.m. ET EIA PADD 2 utilization print (w/e Oct 2) is the quantitative confirm (Sep 25 was 85.6%). Supply healing: Syncrude ~50-day coker TAR wraps ~Oct 5-16 (completion unconfirmed); CNRL 35-day Horizon upgrader TAR implies ~Oct 12-13; Suncor Edmonton/Base fall turnarounds roll off mid-month. All AESO-monitored SAGD cogen units at full MC (01:39 MDT).
changes.conditional: EIA PADD 2 prints high-90s -> snap-back confirmed; prints soft -> Whiting conflict reopens. November apportionment notice ~Oct 19 decides the binding-from-November base case.
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 6, 2026; Reuters Sep 21; in-house maintenance forecast refreshed Oct 5; AESO CSD Oct 7
changes.title: TMW Dec26 widens $0.50 to -$25.25; export arb still healthy

changes.balance: Claims became confirmed strikes on Saudi soil overnight; barrels still flowing; the bypass at capacity; diplomacy stalled. On the ground, the Mocha recapture is contested - treat both sides' claims as unverified.
changes.body: Yemen/Saudi (Oct 6-7): Saudi GACA confirmed Houthi strikes damaged Jazan and Najran airports, wounding three. Houthi claims on Abha, Riyadh's King Khalid airport, and the Aramco Rabigh refinery remain unconfirmed by Riyadh. GCC condemned the Jazan/Najran strikes. Saudi-backed forces say they retook Mocha and are pushing toward Bab el-Mandeb with ~100 coalition jets in support; the Houthis dispute the Mocha claim. Saudi energy minister: East-West pipeline at 5.8 Mb/d (full). Hormuz: UKMTO disclosed five incidents Monday Oct 5 (fresh 1637 UTC strike, engine-room fire); TradeWinds counts 11 ships hit in a week. Ceasefire: stalemate. US buildup timeline stands (three carriers by end-October).
changes.conditional: Confirmed strike on Saudi energy infrastructure -> premium rebuilds; ceasefire proposal advances -> premium bleeds.
changes.delta: Jazan/Najran strikes confirmed by Saudi GACA (3 wounded); Mocha recapture disputed; East-West pipeline full at 5.8 Mb/d
changes.source: Saudi GACA statement, Oct 6, 2026; Reuters, Oct 6, 2026; UKMTO via gCaptain/BOE Report, Oct 5, 2026
changes.title: Riyadh confirms Houthi airport strikes; Mocha contested

changes.balance: The award is the one event that actually reprices barrels today; everything else is headline vol.
changes.body: The SPR exchange bids went in yesterday (40 Mbbl sour: 20 Bryan Mound, 20 Big Hill; Nov-Dec delivery; replacement interest 7.5%/9.5% vs June's 18%). No award announcement has surfaced - the award is the next real data point for Gulf sour pricing; a clean award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf, a no-bid is Sparta's cover-shorts trigger (Sparta Sep 30: Gulf Coast medium grades under pressure into year-end, watching Dec Mars FOB below $1/bbl). Producer news quiet: no updates on the Oct 5 Cenovus-Athabasca C$5.7B deal or the Oct 5 Ithaca-Suncor offshore transaction. RBN Energy's Oct 6 blog (ExxonMobil upstream strategy) flags the Guyana FPSO ramp (+250 kb/d Q4 2026 toward ~1.7 MMb/d by 2030) as the growing Atlantic Basin heavy/medium sour competitor set for Canadian heavy into the USGC.
changes.conditional: Clean award -> Gulf sour repriced softer; no-bid -> Sparta's cover-shorts trigger.
changes.delta: SPR 40 Mbbl bids due Oct 6 11:00 a.m. CT - no award announced; no updates on Cenovus-Athabasca or Ithaca-Suncor deals
changes.source: US DOE SPR solicitation; Sparta Commodities Sep 30; RBN Energy blog Oct 6, 2026
changes.title: SPR bids in (award pending); producer news quiet
